findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the reviewer's disposition when the trigger fires but the plan does not state the enforcement layer (e.g. 'placement unstated -> coach to declare the enforcement seam, do not assert a CLI-only finding'), and add this ambiguous/silent-placement case to the eval alongside the two explicit-placement shapes.
evidence: Trigger: 'deterministic trigger = plan file_impact/scope touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules while naming validation/guard/check work'
Decision rule: 'the reviewer asks where the invariant is enforced and flags CLI-only placement, suggesting the engine seam'

Testing pins only two shapes: 'plan placing validation in CLI-only -> advisory finding fires; plan placing it in engine with CLI delegating -> no finding' — neither covers a plan that names validation/guard work but does NOT state its enforcement layer, which still fires the trigger

Precedent: the existing project.symbol-reference-completeness rubric (.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md) carries an explicit 'Silence about method is not a finding' fallback for exactly this ambiguity class; the plan specifies no analog
findings.finding: The new reviewer criterion specifies a fire/no-fire disposition only for the two explicit-placement plan shapes (validation in CLI-only -> advisory fires; validation in engine with CLI delegating -> no finding), but its deterministic trigger fires on any plan touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules that names 'validation/guard/check' work — including a plan that names such work yet leaves the enforcement LAYER unstated. The reviewer's behavior on that ambiguous/silent-placement case (the incomplete sub-step) is unspecified, so an executor of the criterion has no rule for the input that neither eval shape covers.
findings.location: Approach + Testing/Acceptance Criteria (the reviewer decision rule and the two eval shapes)
scenarios: A plan touches src/rebar/_commands/ and says 'add validation for X' without stating whether the invariant is enforced in the engine or the CLI — the trigger fires but the reviewer has no defined disposition (fire? abstain? coach?)
Two runs of the criterion diverge on the same silent-placement plan because the rubric never defines the fallback, undermining the 'no finding' half of the acceptance eval
findings.suggested_fix: In the criterion rubric, add a fallback clause mirroring the precedent's 'Silence is not a finding' pattern: when validation/guard work is named but the enforcement layer is unstated, emit a coaching prompt to declare where the invariant is enforced rather than asserting CLI-only placement; add a third eval trial for this silent-placement input.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the concrete path prefixes/modules that constitute 'interface modules' in the deterministic trigger (e.g. the MCP/library/reconciler entrypoints named in Context), not just src/rebar/_commands/.
evidence: Trigger says 'interface modules' without a concrete file/path list.
Context enumerates 'the MCP/library/reconciler paths' as the ones that skip validation, but the trigger only concretely names src/rebar/_commands/.
findings.finding: The deterministic trigger names 'src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules' but does not enumerate which modules count as 'interface modules', while the Context names three distinct paths (MCP/library/reconciler) that skip validation.
findings.location: Approach — 'deterministic trigger = ... touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules'
scenarios: An executor building the routing overlay must decide which paths qualify as 'interface modules' to configure the deterministic trigger.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'or interface modules' with an explicit list of path prefixes mapped to the MCP, library, and reconciler surfaces named in the Context section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the criterion is an LLM single_turn finder (per the project.portability dogfood pattern) whose deterministic half is only the file_impact/scope path signal that ROUTES it in, while the validation/guard/check-placement judgment is the LLM's — not a prompt-less DET check like T5a/T7.
evidence: docs/plan-review-gate.md: 'Overlays fire from low-false-positive deterministic triggers where safe (T5a/T5d/T7/T12) and are LLM-routed otherwise. Only the code-grounding set (E4/G1G2/A1/G6) greps the codebase; everything else reasons from the plan text.'

.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md and plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md are both 'execution_mode: single_turn' LLM finders — the dogfood pattern this plan follows is an LLM criterion, not a DET path
The 'naming validation/guard/check work' half is a semantic classification an LLM performs, not a deterministic path/lexicon match
findings.finding: The plan calls its trigger a 'deterministic trigger' but the trigger is a mix of a deterministic file-path signal (file_impact/scope touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules) AND an LLM semantic judgment ('while naming validation/guard/check work'); the criterion is fundamentally an LLM finder (like project.portability / project.symbol-reference-completeness, both execution_mode: single_turn), not a prompt-less DET-routed check like T5a/T5d/T7/T12. The 'deterministic' framing could mislead the implementer into building the wrong routing shape.
findings.location: Approach section: 'deterministic trigger = plan file_impact/scope touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules while naming validation/guard/check work'
scenarios: Implementer wires a prompt-less DET routing entry expecting purely-deterministic firing, then finds the semantic 'validation/guard/check' half needs an LLM finder — rework
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the Approach to 'deterministic ROUTING signal (file_impact/scope touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules) gates in an LLM single_turn finder that judges whether validation/guard/check work is placed CLI-only', mirroring project.portability's routing+prompt split.
